title: Explicit conductor-prepending and its exact specification
statement: Let $X$ be a reduced finite-type rational scheme, with prepared input $P(X)$ and stage count $c_X$ [def-trf-conductor-resolution-preparation]. Given any normalized resolution tower $A$ on $P(X)$ [def-per-qe-normalized-resolution-rule], define $B$ concretely by using $A$ with initial isomorphism composed with $P(X)\to X$ if $D_X$ is unit, and otherwise by adjoining $X$ as a new first level, with center $D_X$, arrow $A_0\to P(X)\to X$, and all subsequent levels, arrows and centers those of $A$. Then $B$ is a normalized resolution tower and satisfies the exact extension predicate: its length is $\operatorname{length}(A)+c_X$, its tail is identified by identity isomorphisms and by identity or successor order embeddings, and its new initial stage, when present, is exactly the conductor stage.

source.place: Exposé VIII, 2.2.3--2.2.9 and 2.3.2--2.3.5(i), printed pp.90--93; agent formalization of the conductor-prepending refinement in the parent proof.

proof.text: Finite-type rational inputs have Noetherian affine rings. The conductor ideal is finitely generated on them. For unit conductor, apply the unit-normal case of the normalized-blowup calculus to see that its map is an isomorphism.

In the nonunit branch define levels, reducedness, centers, arrows and blowup witnesses by Fin.cases, with the original tail initial isomorphism giving the first blowup witness. Coherence and nowhere density are the conductor geometry followed by the tail properties. Nonunit support is nonempty by support_eq_bot_iff. The final level is the original final level, including for a zero-length tail.

Use identity embeddings and isomorphisms in the unit branch and successor embeddings and identity tail isomorphisms in the nonunit branch. The before/after, tail-arrow, tail-center and initial-stage equations reduce to identities and comap_id.
